title: Jonah Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Jonah 3: the second call, the preaching in the great city, the fast of people and animals, and God relenting of the disaster.

questions.text: What does verse 1 say about Yahweh's word coming to Jonah?
questions.explanation: Yahweh's word came to Jonah the second time.

answers.text: It came to him in a dream
It came through another prophet
It came while he was at sea
It came to him a second time

questions.text: What was Jonah to preach in Nineveh?
questions.explanation: He was told to arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that Yahweh would give him.

answers.text: The words of his own choosing
The message that Yahweh gives him
The law given through Moses
A song of thanksgiving

questions.text: How is Nineveh described in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days' journey across.

answers.text: A small town with a low wall
A city of ruins beside the sea
An exceedingly great city, three days across
A city of gardens and vineyards

questions.text: What did Jonah cry out as he entered the city?
questions.explanation: Jonah went a day's journey into the city and cried out that in forty days Nineveh would be overthrown.

answers.text: In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown
Yahweh is gracious and merciful
Turn, and build an altar here
Peace be to this great city

questions.text: What did the people of Nineveh do when they believed God?
questions.explanation: The people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.

answers.text: They drove Jonah out of the city
They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth
They offered many sacrifices of oxen
They shut the gates and kept silent

questions.text: What did the king of Nineveh do when the news reached him?
questions.explanation: He arose from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes.

answers.text: He sent for Jonah at once
He called his army together
He put on sackcloth and sat in ashes
He ordered the gates shut

questions.text: Who was included in the fast that the king proclaimed?
questions.explanation: By the decree of the king and his nobles, neither man nor animal, herd nor flock, was to taste anything or drink water.

answers.text: People and animals alike
Only the king's nobles
Only the men of the city
Only the priests and seers

questions.text: Besides wearing sackcloth, what did the proclamation call for?
questions.explanation: It called for man and animal to be covered with sackcloth, to cry mightily to God, and for everyone to turn from his evil way and from violence.

answers.text: Marching out in arms against Jonah
Bringing gifts of silver to the temple
Keeping the gates shut for forty days
Crying to God and turning from evil and violence

questions.text: What hope did the proclamation express?
questions.explanation: It asked who knows whether God will not turn and relent and turn away from his fierce anger, so that they might not perish.

answers.text: That the city walls would hold out
That God might relent and turn from his anger
That Jonah would come and bless them
That rain would fall on their fields

questions.text: What did God do when he saw that they turned from their evil way?
questions.explanation: God saw their works and relented of the disaster he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

answers.text: He waited forty days more
He sent Jonah away again
He relented and did not do it
He overthrew the city anyway
